newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended higher on Tuesday from New York's previous close on shortcovering as platinum and palladium remained firm, as did silver, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$344.00/50 per ounce on Tuesday, compared to New York's $343.30/70 per ounce close on Monday.
Dealers reported shortcovering that boosted the market.
"There's not too much downside," said one trader.
Gold firmed on the back of steady palladium and platinum, although they remained edgy on Russian deliveries and high swap rates.
Traders saw gold shuttling in a narrow range between $343 and $346 per ounce. Physical demand was said average.
Local gold ended unchanged at HK$3,181 per tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -1.00 from its previous fix at -5.00.
